answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity cheap and verification costly. Every verifier posts a crystal stake; every countersigned invalid transaction is recorded as a delta against the true ledger state and triggers slashing above one full epoch's verifier rewards, so any forged bridge transfer that slips through costs the attacker more than an epoch earns. A sybil must control a validator supermajority to act, since every fake identity carries slashable stake that is destroyed on first detection, making the attack structurally unprofitable.
